cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T9 answers T8 directly, separating historical outcomes from physical causes.
cells.limitation: T2, T5, T8 restate the Geographer's lens without taking up the prior turn.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds salinity as a parameter that could shift the system.
cells.limitation: No mid-debate distinction is used later; T10 and T11 repeat T4's interconnection point.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 and T9 name winds and mountains as rivals to the current.
cells.limitation: Ocean versus westerly-wind heat delivery, and west-versus-east coast exposure, never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T11 tries to fuse current and geography as thread and loom.
cells.limitation: T11 and T12 reach agreement without any view having reshaped another.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D moves from single current to a multi-factor explanation.
cells.limitation: Ending says only 'complex system'; no mechanism is clearer than at T3.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T9 fairly identifies T8's conflation of history with physical cause.
cells.limitation: T3 attacks a 'solely the current' claim nobody in T1 or T2 made.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T6 states a falsifying case: similar currents yet a freezing region.
cells.limitation: T3 and T6 call for tests but name no assumption or concrete test; targets restate.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T9 correctly treats atmospheric circulation as comparably important to the current.
cells.limitation: T2 deterministic civilization claim unsupported; T1 calls a current a stock; T4 loops unnamed.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T12 calls the model an approximation open to revision.
cells.limitation: T2 and T8 assert climate-driven civilizational outcomes as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 grants the Skeptic's point before qualifying it.
cells.limitation: T12 'Agreed' revises nothing; no argument is credited with changing a position.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames the question as current versus wider atmospheric-geographic system.
cells.limitation: Section E recasts the explanation as which focus one prioritizes; T2, T8 drift to history.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T4 contrasts Europe with the Canadian side of the Atlantic.
cells.limitation: No named places at similar latitude are compared; the user's framing stays abstract.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T9 steers back to climate mechanics, the user's actual interest.
cells.limitation: User wanted an explanation; no turn actually explains how heat reaches Europe.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 points to North Atlantic landmass shape as the relevant setting.
cells.limitation: Which coast of Canada is compared is never considered; T8 adds unasked historical stakes.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E offers a route to learn more via climate models.
cells.limitation: Never asks or branches on which places are compared, east or west Canada.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section A names the user's question about ocean versus wider systems.
cells.limitation: What the user wants from the explanation is never explored or offered as alternatives.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: Section D challenges the popular single 'magic' current assumption.
cells.limitation: The similar-latitude comparison itself, and coast exposure, are never examined as assumptions.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E contrasts focusing on heat flow versus structural constraints.
cells.limitation: No conflict of what matters to the user in understanding this is surfaced.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 flags confirmation bias toward the textbook Gulf Stream account.
cells.limitation: Received wisdom is named once and not developed into something the user can reflect on.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E leaves the user a way to investigate further.
cells.limitation: Few distinctions the user could accept or reject; closing is generic 'complex system'.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: T3 and T9 list current, mountains and prevailing winds as candidate explanations.
cells.limitation: Candidates named but never stated as distinct mechanisms with their causal paths.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T9 weighs current against atmospheric circulation as comparably vital.
cells.limitation: What each explanation costs in evidence or fails to account for is never said.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E proposes models removing the Gulf Stream to isolate its contribution.
cells.limitation: Section E ends on which focus one prioritizes; no observable comparison like west-coast Canada.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T12 notes the understanding is approximate and revisable.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns, like the current's share versus winds, are not separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: examine climate models simulating removal of the Gulf Stream.
cells.limitation: No simpler concrete thing to look at, such as comparing coastal temperature records.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 is plain: historical outcomes versus physical causes.
cells.limitation: T7, T10 lean on 'emergent behavior', 'multi-loop', 'parameter' without concrete meaning.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T9 clearly targets T8's historical claim.
cells.limitation: T6 'our hypothesis' and T7 'That' have unclear referents.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Turns are near-identical in length, giving a flat cadence.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Each mind has a labelled lens: systems, history, falsifiability.
cells.limitation: One shared register across all three; no explicit change of position anywhere.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T9 is economical and redirects the debate.
cells.limitation: T4, T10, T11 repeat the interconnected-system point without adding content.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T8 versus T9 sets history against physical mechanism.
cells.limitation: Tension stays abstract; the puzzle of mild Europe and frozen Canada is never dramatised.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T12 claims movement from a simple causal claim.
cells.limitation: No reversal occurs; T12's agreement names no argument that changed anyone.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T3 Skeptic opens sharply: 'Be careful.'
cells.limitation: Minds speak in the same neutral register; personality rests on labels.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T11: the current is the thread, geography the loom.
cells.limitation: The only analogy is a familiar one; no vivid example of a real place.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T9 briefly sharpens the exchange by calling out conflation.
cells.limitation: Uniform intensity and rhythm from T1 to T12; nothing builds.

strengths: T9 Skeptic cleanly separates historical outcomes from physical causes and refocuses the debate.
Section D corrects the popular single-current explanation toward a multi-factor account.
Section E proposes a specific test: models removing the Gulf Stream to isolate its share.
weaknesses: All minds name winds and mountains but never explain how westerly winds carry ocean heat onto Europe.
Historical Geographer in T2, T5, T8 drifts into unsupported environmental determinism off the question.
T11 and T12 reach agreement with no argument credited for any change; Section E ends on prioritization.

symptoms.observed: Atmospheric circulation is named as vital but its mechanism is never explained.
symptoms.evidence: the atmospheric circulation patterns are just as vital to the equation

symptoms.observed: Section E ends on which focus one prioritizes rather than a deciding observation.
symptoms.evidence: depends on whether one prioritizes the mechanical flow of heat

symptoms.observed: Unsupported deterministic civilization claims, outside the climate question asked.
symptoms.evidence: European civilizations to flourish where others at the same latitude remained frozen

symptoms.observed: Agreement declared without any argument changing a position.
symptoms.evidence: Agreed. We have moved from a simple causal claim

symptoms.observed: Interconnected-system point restated three times without new content.
symptoms.evidence: it is a multi-loop system. We cannot isolate the current

findings.description: Claims winter warmth let European civilizations flourish where others at the same latitude stayed frozen; no support, deterministic.
Sentence presented as Huntington's own words via 'As I have argued'; may not be verbatim from the book.
Calls the Gulf Stream a stock of energy; in the cited systems vocabulary a moving current is a flow.
Asserts reinforcing loops maintain the warmth without identifying any reinforcing loop.

rubric_fit_notes: A general science question with no personal context gives C3 and C4 little material; low ratings there reflect missed opportunities (asking which places are compared) but the fit is loose. Whether the T2 Huntington line is verbatim is unknown to me.
raw.question_type_note: Read as exploratory: C4 as examination of the single-current assumption and C5 as settling between ocean and atmospheric explanations; Section E's prioritization framing cost C3.1 and C5.3.
